headword: {韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}

definitions.explanation: Food and cooking traditions originating from Korea.

examples.japanese: {韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}が{好|す}きだ。
{駅前|えきまえ}に{新|あたら}しい{韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}の{店|みせ}ができた。
examples.english: A new Korean restaurant opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}の{日本|にほん}では{韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}ブームが{続|つづ}いていて、チーズタッカルビやヤンニョムチキンが{特|とく}に{人気|にんき}だ。
examples.english: In recent Japan, the Korean food boom continues, with cheese dakgalbi and yangnyeom chicken being especially popular.

notes:
A compound of {韓国|かんこく} (South Korea) and {料理|りょうり} (cooking, cuisine). Korean food has become extremely popular in Japan, particularly among younger generations, driven by K-pop and Korean drama cultural influence (the so-called {韓流|かんりゅう} boom).

Common Korean dishes well known in Japan include キムチ (kimchi), ビビンバ (bibimbap), サムギョプサル (samgyeopsal), and チヂミ (jijim, Korean pancakes).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}の{店|みせ}: Korean restaurant
- {韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}を{食|た}べる: to eat Korean food
- {本格的|ほんかくてき}な{韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}: authentic Korean cuisine
- {韓国料理|かんこくりょうり}{教室|きょうしつ}: Korean cooking class

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {中華料理|ちゅうかりょうり}: Chinese cuisine — another extremely popular foreign cuisine in Japan
- {和食|わしょく}: Japanese cuisine — the native culinary tradition
- {洋食|ようしょく}: Western-style food — Western dishes adapted to Japanese tastes
